$$\mathbf{r} = [(t + \sin 2t)\,\mathbf{i} + (\cos 2t)\,\mathbf{j}]\ \mathrm{m}.$$

Find, when $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$,

Question 1 (d) : le sujet dit que Q a la vitesse (-i + 2j) m s^-1 « in the same direction as P », mais la vitesse de P à t = pi/4 est i - 2j, exactement l'opposée : les deux vecteurs sont colinéaires de sens contraire. Résolu avec la valeur imprimée (vitesse relative 2i - 4j) ; la remarque est dans le corrigé.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Setting up.** $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are unit vectors along fixed perpendicular axes, so velocity and acceleration are the first and second derivatives of the position vector with respect to $t$ (chain rule on $\sin 2t$ and $\cos 2t$):

$$\mathbf{r} = (t + \sin 2t)\,\mathbf{i} + (\cos 2t)\,\mathbf{j}$$

$$\mathbf{v} = \frac{d\mathbf{r}}{dt} = (1 + 2\cos 2t)\,\mathbf{i} - 2\sin 2t\,\mathbf{j}\ \ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

$$\mathbf{a} = \frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt} = -4\sin 2t\,\mathbf{i} - 4\cos 2t\,\mathbf{j}\ \ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

At $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ we have $2t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $\sin 2t = 1$ and $\cos 2t = 0$:

$$\mathbf{a}\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = -4(1)\,\mathbf{i} - 4(0)\,\mathbf{j} = -4\,\mathbf{i}\ \ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

**The acceleration at $t = \pi/4$ is $\mathbf{a} = -4\,\mathbf{i}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$** (magnitude $4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, in the negative $x$-direction). The velocity at this instant, needed later, is $\mathbf{v}\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = (1+0)\,\mathbf{i} - 2(1)\,\mathbf{j} = (\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: the magnitude of the force acting on $P$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
By Newton's second law, $\mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a}$ with $m = 3\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $\mathbf{a} = -4\,\mathbf{i}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ from part (a):

$$\mathbf{F} = 3(-4\,\mathbf{i}) = -12\,\mathbf{i}\ \mathrm{N}$$

$$|\mathbf{F}| = 12\ \mathrm{N}$$

**The magnitude of the force is $12\ \mathrm{N}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the magnitude of the momentum of the particle.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The momentum is $\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v}$. From part (a), $\mathbf{v}\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, so

$$\mathbf{p} = 3(\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j}) = (3\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$$

$$|\mathbf{p}| = \sqrt{3^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5} \approx 6.71\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$$

**The magnitude of the momentum is $3\sqrt{5} \approx 6.71\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Another particle $Q$ is moving with velocity $\mathbf{v} = (-\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in the same direction as $P$. Find the velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ when $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Relative velocity.** The velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ is $\mathbf{v}_P - \mathbf{v}_Q$.

At $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$: $\mathbf{v}_P = \mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j}$ (part (a)) and, as printed, $\mathbf{v}_Q = -\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}$. Hence

$$\mathbf{v}_P - \mathbf{v}_Q = (\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j}) - (-\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}) = (2\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

Its magnitude is $\sqrt{2^2 + 4^2} = 2\sqrt{5} \approx 4.47\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

**The velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$ is $(2\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.**

**Remark on the wording.** The printed velocity of $Q$ is exactly $-\mathbf{v}_P$: $Q$ moves along the same line as $P$ but in the opposite sense, so the phrase "in the same direction as $P$" can only mean "along the same straight line". Had $Q$ really had the same velocity as $P$, the relative velocity would be $\mathbf{0}$, which would make the question trivial. The printed vector is used here.
